company_summary: Northwind Analytics is a 12-person consultancy in Chicago. It helps regional manufacturers replace spreadsheet reporting with a shared set of numbers.
services_offered: Metric definitions for plant and finance teams
pain_points: Weekly client reports are assembled in spreadsheets, so the Monday leadership pack depends on someone copying numbers out of three systems.
The planning tool, the plant system, and the finance workbook do not share one definition of a metric.
Analyst time goes to refreshing the pack instead of explaining what changed.
ai_opportunities: A scheduled pull from the three source systems would remove the copy step the services page describes.
A short metric dictionary, written once per client, would keep a dashboard from mixing two definitions of the same number.
A Monday note that flags only the metrics that moved would leave the analysts time to write the interpretation.
value_proposition: The useful conversation is which of the three sources should refresh on a schedule, and which numbers need one definition before anything is automated.
recommended_angle: The Monday leadership pack that is still copied out of three systems.

evidence.claim: The weekly client pack is still assembled by copying numbers.
evidence.quote: Weekly client reports are assembled in spreadsheets.

evidence.claim: One leadership pack is fed by three systems.
evidence.quote: The Monday leadership pack is still copied out of three systems.

inferences.claim: A scheduled pull from those sources would remove the copy step.
inferences.basis: The services page describes an analyst pasting numbers from three sources. It does not say the firm wants that automated.
